what_happened: The person running Athena renewed the the person running Athena claim while a landing was rebuilding Athena. Renewing writes the person running Athena/Claim.toml into the shared working tree. That left the tree dirty, and the rebuild after a landing needs a clean tree, so the rebuild refused and the batch stopped. No job work was judged bad.
cause: Athena lets the person running Athena commands write into the working tree that drain and landing use, and nothing tells the command that a landing is in progress or blocks it. The rebuild's clean-tree rule is checked only when the rebuild runs. Safe use depends on the person running Athena remembering when not to run such commands. This is the same cause as the other hand-command mistakes: the person acts on shared state without Athena showing or guarding its current state.
prevention: Make the claim-renew command check for a landing or rebuild in progress (a landing marker or lock) and refuse, or wait, with a clear message. Better still, keep Claim.toml out of the tracked working tree, or have the rebuild's clean-tree check ignore that file. Add a test that renewing during a landing neither dirties the tree nor stops the rebuild.
proposed_request: Make `athena` claim renewal safe during a landing. Outcome: renewing the the person running Athena claim while a landing or rebuild is in progress never leaves the shared working tree dirty and never makes the post-landing rebuild refuse. Either the renew command detects a landing in progress and waits or refuses with a plain message, or the claim file is kept where the rebuild's clean-tree check does not see it. Acceptance: (1) a test that starts a simulated landing, runs claim renewal, and shows the rebuild still succeeds; (2) renewal outside a landing still works and the claim is valid; (3) the message names the reason when renewal is refused; (4) a changelog entry is added.
